messages:
sam_customer: Hey team — just onboarded a new SSO-provisioned service account for tenant t-9a2f. Calls to /v1/generate and /v1/rerank are returning 403 with 'missing_scope'. Worked earlier with manual key. Can we triage?

maya_cs: sorry you're hitting this. can you paste the exact curl you used and the 403 body?

sam_customer: sure — reproducer below:

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/rerank \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer eyJ...svc" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"queries": ["q1"], "documents": ["d1"]}'
```

Response:
```json
{"error":"forbidden","message":"token missing permission: rerank","code":403}
```

sam_customer: note: our IdP provisioning CSV uses semicolon-delimited scopes because some provisioning tooling expects that.

maya_cs: thanks. forwarding to infra to check the provisioner parsing. tagging jon.

jon_infra: looking at the provisioner logs for tenant t-9a2f — I can see the claim that arrived from the provisioner: scopes claim = '"generate;rerank;embeddings"' (note the quotes). Our claim parser currently splits on commas only, and then strips quotes naive-ly which leaves a single token with embedded semicolons. runtime treats that as an unknown scope and drops it from allowed perms. that maps to missing rerank/generate.

riley_prod: ugh. so the token ends up with no recognized scopes? explains why manual UI-created keys (space-separated) worked.

jon_infra: yep. repro steps I used locally:

1) create JWT with claim: 
```json
{"sub":"svc:t-9a2f:sa-77","scopes":"\"generate;rerank;embeddings\""}
```
2) call /v1/generate -> 403 missing permission: generate

jon_infra: quick mitigation: create an org service key via Console or the keys API specifying scopes as a list or space/comma separated string. temporary patch: run this API to fix existing tokens for the tenant:

```bash
# replace with tenant and svc id
curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/admin/tenants/t-9a2f/keys/fix-scopes \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"svc_id":"sa-77","scopes":"generate,rerank,embeddings"}'
```

maya_cs: jon — can we offer the customer a single-use workaround (manual key) while you push a fix?

jon_infra: yes — created a one-off key for sam_customer with explicit scopes; sent the key via secure channel. also opened internal PR to update provisioner CSV parsing to accept semicolons and quoted entries: GH#3421.

deploy-bot: Deploy queued: infra/provisioner-accept-semicolons GH#3421 (sha: ab12cd)

jon_infra: rolling patch to staging now. patch will: split on /[\n\t\s,;]+/ and trim quotes, and add a unit test for quoted semicolon lists. should prevent future CSVs from producing a single unrecognized token.

riley_prod: once deployed, we should run a migration to normalize existing tenant claims that still have semicolons/quotes. can we schedule that in the change?

jon_infra: yes — migration script in PR; will run after staging smoke tests. ETA for production deploy ~ 40m.

sam_customer: thanks all. the one-off key works and unblocks our rollout. please keep me posted on prod deploy.

deploy-bot: Deploy succeeded: infra/provisioner-accept-semicolons GH#3421 to production (2026-03-17T14:12:12Z) :tada:

maya_cs: thanks for confirming — marking as escalated->resolved. follow-up: we'll add a note to the SSO onboarding doc to call out acceptable scope delimiters and update the CSV template.

sam_customer: appreciated. small ask — can you also add a healthcheck alert when a tenant has >50% of tokens without generate/rerank perms? early detection would help.

riley_prod: good idea. created tracking ticket INFRA-1286 to add the alert and link onboarding doc.

sam_customer: :thumbsup:

maya_cs: closing thread. reach out if anything flares back up.
